newsitem.title: BRAZIL: NET Brasil calls worldwide digital set box tender.
newsitem.headline: NET Brasil calls worldwide digital set box tender.

text.p: NET Brasil, an Organizacoes Globo subisidiary, has invited 80 companies worldwide to tender for the manufacture of at least 500,000 digital television set top boxes as part of an ambitious new pay television expansion program.

In a news conference, NET Brasil's chief executive officer, Moyses Pluciennik, said the new digital set top boxes would provide full connectivity for a wide range of information and entertainment services to be offered to Brazil's booming pay-TV market.
He said the development and manufacture of the new set top boxes, to be named NET Bhest boxes, will require a first year investment of over $150 million.

Pluciennik said 1.8 million Brazilian households already took pay-TV services but nationwide penetration levels were low at just five percent, compared with levels of 55 percent in neighboring Argentina and 71 percent in the United States.
"This market is exploding and its growth potential continues to be enormous," he said, adding that NET Brasil's customer base was growing at a rate of 100,000 households a month.
Pluciennik said NET Brasil's network controlled 70 percent of the Brazilian pay-TV market, delivering programming through a mix of cable, satellite and local wireless television services.

NET Brasil's technical director Luis Fernando Baptistella said the set top boxes would be sold to operators at prices ranging between $150 to $300, which he said were relatively low if measured by international standards.
"We can afford to be aggresive with our prices because our volume is very aggresive," said Baptistella.
Baptistella said NET Brasil's order of 500,000 digital set top units, which could be increased to one million, would be the largest ever made by any group of pay-TV operators.
No retail price for the boxes has yet been determined.
Baptistella said manufacturers would be asked to present their proposals by March, field tests would begin in June and commercial delivery of the units should commence by October.
Pluciennik said the NET Bhest boxes would at first just exploit pay-TV services, including regular cable programming, Pay-Per-View and Near Home Video on Demand.

However he said that in the future the company would seek to squeeze the most out of the boxes' capacity by offering a full range of digitally delivered products from computer services to home banking.
"The boxes allow for a huge variety of marketing possibilities. Pay TV is just a first step," he said.
